tagline: Europe's most surprising comeback — a once-grey communist capital painted in rainbows, ringed by bunkers and mountains.
overview: Tirana spent 45 years sealed inside Europe's most paranoid dictatorship — then exploded into colour. Mayor-turned-painter Edi Rama had the drab communist blocks painted in bold patterns, and the city has been repainting itself ever since.

The symbols of isolation are now the attractions: Bunk'Art turns the regime's giant nuclear bunkers into museums, Skanderbeg Square was repaved as a stone pedestrian plain, and the Pyramid — a mausoleum for the dictator — was rebuilt as a climbable tech hub.
Speed's 2024 tour streamed from Tirana. From the centre, the Dajti Express cable car climbs a mountain in 15 minutes, and the Albanian Riviera's beaches are a few hours south.

funFacts.title: THE PAINTED CITY
funFacts.text: Post-2000 the mayor had drab blocks painted in bright patterns — the city has been colorful ever since.

funFacts.title: 750,000 BUNKERS
funFacts.text: Albania's regime built a bunker for every few citizens — Tirana's biggest are now museums.

funFacts.title: THE PYRAMID REBORN
funFacts.text: The dictator's abandoned mausoleum reopened as a climbable tech and youth centre.

funFacts.title: BUNK'ART
funFacts.text: Cold War nuclear bunkers under the outskirts are now history-and-art museums.

funFacts.title: SKANDERBEG SQUARE
funFacts.text: The huge pedestrian plaza was repaved with stones from every Albanian district.

funFacts.title: DAJTI EXPRESS
funFacts.text: A cable car climbs 1,613m Dajti mountain from the city edge — longest in the Balkans.

funFacts.title: COFFEE NATION
funFacts.text: Albanians drink more café coffee per capita than almost any European nation.

funFacts.title: BESA
funFacts.text: The Albanian code of honour — besa, the given word — sheltered Jews through WWII.

funFacts.title: THE ISOLATED DECADES
funFacts.text: For 45 years Albania was Europe's most closed country — the transformation is the story.
